title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: index browser, schema and errors for custom connectors in the admin centre
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, administrator paths, role-assignment API and error-download script are supported. It distinguishes the documented views from the overdue roadmap target and appropriately limits the Copilot Visibility control to its documented partner-connector scope.

claims.quote: View index browser, schema, and the errors for custom connectors from the M365 Admin center for better troubleshooting.

claims.claim: Schema recommendations are provided in the admin center for published custom connectors.

claims.claim: Schema recommendations check for a missing title semantic label.
claims.quote: Schema recommendations currently check for four missing semantic labels: title

claims.claim: Schema recommendations check for a missing url semantic label.
claims.quote: url – Identifies the canonical link to the source item. Required for Copilot citations to link back to the source system.

claims.claim: Schema recommendations check for a missing lastModifiedBy semantic label.
claims.quote: lastModifiedBy – Identifies who last updated an item. Improves attribution in Copilot responses.

claims.claim: Schema recommendations check for a missing lastModifiedDateTime semantic label.
claims.quote: lastModifiedDateTime – Indicates when an item was last updated. Enables Copilot to reason over recency and answer time-based questions.

claims.claim: Microsoft's connector documentation says access and management require the AI administrator role.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is a privileged Microsoft Entra role.

claims.quote: Assign the AI Administrator role to users who need to do the following tasks: Manage all aspects of Microsoft Copilot

claims.claim: Microsoft states that updating a connection's configured access permissions after creation is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft's documented remedy for unintended connection access permissions is deleting and recreating the connection with explicit permissions.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.claim: User or group permission changes can take up to 24 hours to appear in Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Changes to user or group permissions (ACLs) might take up to 24 hours to reflect in Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Permissions updates occur during a full crawl.
claims.quote: Permissions updates occur during a full crawl, not an incremental crawl.

claims.claim: An incremental crawl does not apply permissions updates, so source changes can remain absent from the index until a full crawl.
claims.quote: Permissions updates occur during a full crawl, not an incremental crawl. If your data source permissions change after the last full crawl, you must trigger a new full crawl on-demand or schedule it to update the index.
